content.thinking:
I need to write this file in one careful pass without verification, designing a Genshin-style lava golem with dark basalt plates, glowing molten orange seams, and gold filigree pyro accents, standing around 2.6 meters tall to tower over a human. I'll stick to well-known, reliable API patterns since I can't typecheck as I go.

I'm sketching the skeleton: hips root, a spine chain of three joints up to the chest, then a neck chain leading to a head tip joint, with a jaw joint parented off the head aimed forward. For the arms I'm planning wide shoulder placements and oversized limb proportions to match the golem's massive build.

Setting s=1 for left side with explicit parent joints, then tuning the sweep radii for a chunky arm that tapers toward the wrist before flaring into a fist.

For the hands I'll build a dodecahedron-ish fist shape with knuckle boxes and a thumb, then add fingers as short two-joint chains parented to the wrist tip, sweeping hexagonal cross-sections to keep them thick and rigid within the joint budget.

Now I'm working out the leg structure: hip, knee, and ankle joints positioned with forward-bending knees, connected as a three-point chain, with the foot attached at the ankle tip including a block-shaped foot and separate toe boxes. The hip chain parents back to the root joint.

Then I'm setting up the torso by lofting the body along the spine, defining pelvis, waist, and chest cross-sections with widths and depths that map to the x and z axes along the vertical path, chaining the hips and spine bones together.

For the shoulder pauldrons, I'm planning big basalt rock masses using scaled icosahedron geometry at the shoulder joints, with gold crescent trim and glowing lava crack details on the surface.

For paint schemes, I'm defining a mottled basalt cel-paint and a scaled-plate paint with dark seams, then thinking about how to render lava vein cracks on the torso using vivid orange coloring since the paint itself can't glow — I'll need a separate glow layer for that emissive effect.

Still writing paint functions...

I'm also adding gold trim and lava glow colors for the pyro aesthetic, plus flame/ember card effects rising from shoulders and back using glow(). For the chest, I'm planning a glowing lava core framed by a gold ring, positioned at the chest front.

Now I'm figuring out radiating gold vein lines from the core outward across the chest surface, using drape to conform them to the torso shape.

Now I'm designing the head as a blocky basalt faceted form set low into the shoulders, using a faceted icosahedron shape scaled down, with glowing slit eyes, a dark brow ridge slab, and a separate jaw piece featuring glowing mouth interior and small spike teeth.

I'm figuring out the eye geometry: extruded glowing slanted slits in yellow-white with orange rims, oriented to face forward, and tracing the neck's curved path up to where the head joint sits so the head aims upward and forward along that tangent.

Now I'm setting the head box dimensions and double-checking the torso's top height against its rounded cap — realizing the default round cap dome adds extra height that pushes the torso top too far up, so I need to either flatten the caps or shrink the last loft station to keep proportions sane.

I'll switch to flat caps for the torso loft so the top ends cleanly at the chosen height, letting pauldrons and the head cover the seam, and the pelvis bottom flat cap works fine since the legs cover it. I'm laying out five torso stations from pelvis to trapezius with increasing then narrowing widths to form the hips, waist, chest, and shoulders, using Catmull interpolation between them, ending flat at the trapezius height — then positioning the head center just above that.

Now I'm working out the neck chain geometry and head placement: the neck sweeps up through a few points to a joint tip, then the head box sits centered a bit higher with its own half-width, half-height, and half-depth, positioning the eyes toward the front face. I'm considering using a chunkier rock-like geometry for the head instead of a plain box, while also tracking total figure height with horns, crest, and flames to make sure the golem reads as towering over a human, even though I can't actually measure it without running the code.

Still working out skull and jaw geometry...

I'll add a small glowing box inside the jaw for the mouth interior, tinted orange, then build teeth as spikes pointing down from the upper jaw and up from the lower jaw along the front edge.

Now I'm working on the horns, sweeping curved obsidian shapes that taper from a flat base to a pointed tip, attached to the head bone and angled back from the skull.

I'm also thinking about giving the golem a basalt identity: hexagonal prism columns clustered along the head and neck crest, with shoulders built from fanned bundles of varying-height hex columns as pauldrons, and planning a reusable helper function to generate these basalt column parts.

I want some columns to have thin glowing hex-disk caps at the top to suggest pooled lava, which adds nice detail without too much geometry overhead. I'm keeping part counts in the hundreds via loops, and limiting flat material colors to a tight palette — a few lava tones, gold, bone, ink — staying well under the 64-color budget since paint layers don't count against that limit.

For gold, I'm using a baked two-tone paint and applying it to trim pieces: wrist rings, shoulder crescents, belt, chest frame, and crown tassels styled like hanging card-tassels off the belt with cords in red/orange. I'm also planning two textures — a layered flame teardrop shape for glowing cards, and small ember-spark circles — plus a cluster of tiny floating glowing octahedrons around the golem as an elemental motif, while making sure nothing ends up floating above the figure's silhouette.

For the pyro emblem, I'm thinking of placing a gold-outlined flame-in-diamond glyph as a decal on the back torso plate, with a transparent cutout background so it reads as etched metal rather than glowing paint, and considering a small forehead gem as an alternative focal point. I'm also sketching a gold collar loop around the chest using the hip joint's bone axis as a reference plane for alignment.

Working through the belt now, I'm building it from a closed-loop sweep around a literal point near the pelvis rather than relying on the hip joint's orientation, since the torso surface is defined by its own sweep and stays independent from leg geometry. I'm setting the belt's cross-section as a thin circular radius for a sleek metallic band, and considering a second loop elsewhere on the torso for additional detailing.

I'm also planning the gold buckle as a lathed disc centered on the belt front, and sketching hanging loincloth plates as extruded trapezoid slabs attached at the belt front and back, giving them a stone-tablet look with glowing rune accents and gold trim, positioned symmetrically along the belt's outer z-offset.

I'm placing three front plates and two back plates sized and spaced to clear the thigh and knee geometry, checking their hang length against leg positions so they don't clip, and orienting the extrusion so the thickness runs along z while the outline sits in the x-y plane.

For tassels, I'm framing cards at the belt with a flipped orientation and flow direction, sizing them around 0.07 by 0.3, and positioning four of them at the hip sides near the bone attachment point. For the legs, I'm setting up tapered radius arrays for the thigh sweep, narrowing from a wider top radius down toward the knee across multiple keyframes.

Now I'm adding knee armor with a hex-column icosahedron piece, gold greave bands at the ankles, and foot blocks sized roughly 0.34 wide by 0.18 tall by 0.55 long positioned at the ankle joint with a slight sink into the ground for visual grounding, followed by three hex-prism cylindrical toes extending forward from the foot.

I need to make sure the ankle sits correctly within the shin sweep, which tapers down to y=0.2 with a rounded cap, and the foot box covers that transition point cleanly.

Now I'm working out the arm rig: shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints positioned to create roughly 0.7 and 0.68 length segments, with fists hanging below the wrists and the arms spread wide enough to avoid intersecting the legs, plus setting up the sweep radius taper for the arm limb.

Thickening the forearm taper for a bulkier golem look, then adding gold cuff rings using a torus oriented along the arm axis, and considering hex-plate armor scattered along the forearm surface.

Scattering small cylindrical rock studs across torso, arms, legs, and back as basalt plating, then adding a glowing molten crack seam running along the arm using a swept line path.

I need the seam to bend with the arm rather than stay rigid, so I'm binding the sweep's path to the arm bone chain for proper deformation, and doing the same for the legs with the crack line placed along the front of the thigh and shin, adjusting the angle to face the right side depending on limb orientation.

For the orange glow strip on the arm, I'm adding a thin emissive seam line, maybe splitting it into two segments at different angles for visual variation, and reducing the sweep's polygon count to keep triangle counts low. I'll also plan to add lava veins on the torso using the drape technique.

I'm now thinking about placing a cluster of hexagonal columns along the spine on the back, angled upward and outward from the surface, anchored to the nearest spine joint. I need to make sure these columns don't visually clash with the back emblem decal, so I'm repositioning them to the sides near the upper back instead.

Next I'm designing rising flame card elements attached near the shoulders and upper back, using frame-based card rendering with varied sizes and glow intensity, placing clusters on the pauldrons and around the upper back and head.

I'm also adding floating ember sparks as small glowing octahedra scattered in a ring around the figure, keeping the count modest (around 10) and sized small for subtlety, drawing on the pyro motif.

For the eyes, I'm extruding an angled slit-shaped outline with mirrored geometry for each side, making sure the thickness is centered on the plane so both faces render correctly regardless of the mirrored direction.

Checking the brow slant direction confirms angry brows dip toward the center, so inner-low outer-high is correct for both eyes, keeping outline point ordering consistent.

I'm plotting the eyebrow shape as a non-crossing polygon with inner tip, midpoint, outer tip, and bottom points, giving it a warm glow color, then positioning the eyes and figuring out the front z-plane of the head box for depth placement.

Now I'm adding a brow ridge above the eyes using a sloped dark wedge shape, meeting at the center for a unibrow effect, and skipping a nose while planning cheek rock details and a glowing mouth. Then I move on to thinking about a gold circlet or band around the head's crown.

I'm sketching a glowing forehead gem as a scaled octahedron in warm red-orange, plus gold ring accents on the horns like tassels, and roughing out box dimensions for the head geometry while checking how it connects to the neck.

For the neck I'm placing a short cylinder joint right below the head, then adding hexagonal cheek columns flanking the head like ears, angled outward and back. For the shoulders, I'm planning an icosahedron base rock with three fanned hex columns pointing up and out, wrapped with a gold ring torus at the base to form crescent-style pauldrons.

Writing crescent outline points...

I'll settle on placing it at s*1.07 for a snug embed, and instead decide to use a decal for the gold filigree swirl pattern on the pauldron surface rather than a separate plate—projecting a gold scroll-and-circle SVG design onto the faceted icosahedron.

Planning out the remaining ornamental SVGs: a gold emblem ring with a central flame glyph for the back, a layered flame texture (orange outer, yellow inner, white tip), and a small tasseled cord design with gold cap and strands.

I'm also tallying joint counts across the rig—spine, neck, jaw, arms, fingers, thumbs, legs—landing around fifty joints total, with finger geometry handled via three-point chains.

Still writing finger and wrist details...

Still positioning finger geometry...

I'm plotting the thumb's angle pointing forward and down from the palm, then naming each finger segment by hand side (L/R). For visual detail I'm adding small obsidian spikes on the fist knuckles, and now I'm setting up the lava color palette for the cel-shaded crack paint effect.

For the cracked rock texture, I'm defining a function that uses Voronoi cell distances to create glowing crack lines -- where the gap between nearest cells is small, it shows bright lava core colors fading to ember, otherwise it renders as dark rock, all masked by a noise function to vary where cracks appear.

Setting bone and teeth colors next, then horns with obsidian and gold ring accents. Writing a reusable column helper for building limb/bone segments with position, direction, length, radius, and paint parameters.

I'm double-checking the type imports and confirming the Fill and Joint types are correctly exported, plus verifying that the glow and paint logic handles colors properly per part.

I'm estimating texel density for a 3m golem with a large painted surface area to decide on a 2048 paint size with a 4096 atlas, making sure crack details stay crisp despite many small painted parts consuming texture space. I'm also checking how the glow function clones materials for tinted card textures.

Now I'm writing the import statements for the scene, making sure every imported module—frame, limb, rng, bezier, catmull, polyline, cells, noise, paint, scales, svg, cel, glow, Fill, and Joint—actually gets used somewhere to avoid unused-import errors, since things like smoothstep won't be needed.

Building the skeleton hierarchy...

Continuing the chain with neck1, neck2, and head joints parented off the chest, with head set as the neck chain's tip -- I check that the neck start sits reasonably above the chest joint. Now I'm starting the jaw joint, parented to the head.

Then I set up the torso loft, binding the sweep to the hips, spine, and neck bones with flat caps and the crack paint, verifying the station path y-values line up with the spine chain's extent. I'm now starting the loop for building the arms symmetrically on both sides.

Tuning the arm sweep radius keyframes...

Lifting the seam point slightly should keep it clean near the elbow. For the shoulder I'm adding a pauldron using an icosahedron attached to the shoulder joint, scaled flatter for an armor-like look, and considering whether to vary its rotation for visual interest.

Now I'm working out a fan of spikes around the shoulder, computing base positions and direction vectors for each one; I notice the tallest spike's length would push its tip too high, so I need to shorten it.

Adjusting the lengths down, scaling thickness, and checking that the pauldron base and spike tips sit below the head height, which they now do with room to spare.

I'm adding a gold ring torus around the pauldron base, rotated flat to lay horizontal, and briefly considering a gold crescent decal before deciding to skip it.

I'm placing small flame-shaped card frames at each shoulder, angled and leaning slightly backward with a subtle flow direction, then adding stud details scattered along the upper arm tube before moving on to build the leg chain geometry from hip to foot points.

Writing leg chain parameters...

Adjusting the ankle torus sizing, then moving to the foot box geometry and toe cylinders, keeping the bone attachment on the leg tip for proper rigging.

Checking the toe cylinders sit flush with the foot bottom, then sketching a belt loop sweep around the torso using a gold paint for the sculpted trim.

Adding more trim loops now — a thin lava-glow strip near the hip, a gold chest band under the pecs, a waist strap, and a collar ring — then working out the chest's front z-offset at different heights to keep the torso profile consistent.

Now I'm designing the chest's focal ornament: a glowing orange core sphere nested with a brighter yellow-white inner sphere, framed by a gold torus ring sitting flush against the chest surface, and surrounding that with eight small gold spikes radiating outward like petals.

I'm also sketching vein paths that drape from the core outward across the chest and shoulder, defining mirrored control points for how they curve and follow the body's surface.

Now I'm adding glowing lava sides, then moving to the back of the model: a dorsal ridge of five hexagonal columns along the spine, sized larger toward the top, with glowing caps, positioning their bases to embed slightly into the back surface at each height station.

I realize the dorsal columns at the centerline will collide with the emblem decal I'd placed around y=1.6, so I'm reconsidering shifting the emblem lower, maybe to y=1.2, to avoid overlap.

Actually, I'll drop the back-mounted emblem entirely and instead put it on the belt buckle facing forward—a small plane with the emblem texture positioned just in front of a gold diamond-shaped buckle shield, which solves the placement conflict cleanly.

Now I'm working out the loincloth plates hanging from the belt, extruding a tapered outline that narrows from the hip down to a point, positioned on either side of the buckle so they don't overlap it.

Placing a center plate under the buckle and back plates symmetrically, I check that thighs clear the plate positions without overlap issues. For detailing, I'm adding a thin gold trim and a small stud sphere for accent, plus tassel frames hanging from the belt sides.

Now I'm defining the head geometry: a main box for the skull shape, cheek wedges, top plates angled slightly, and a gold crown band around the head.

I'm checking that the band position doesn't collide with the brow and eye placement, adjusting the y-coordinates so the forehead band sits above the brow line, with eyes centered slightly below.

Now I'm placing a forehead gem on the gold band, positioning it so it slightly overlaps the brow without clashing, then working out the face geometry below the eyes down to the jaw, adding a thin glowing slab near the mouth area.

I'm deciding to tilt the jaw open slightly by posing it after all jaw parts are built, since geometry moves rigidly with later poses — using a small forward rotation around the jaw's pivot to create a readable open-mouth look, calculating how far the chin tip shifts at that angle.

Now I'm placing teeth as small cones along the upper and lower jaw edges, adding curved tusks jutting from the jaw sides, and sizing the jaw box itself so the chin extends slightly past the head's front face, with a glowing lava slab box fitted inside the mouth cavity for the ember effect.

Good, that'll reveal the mouth properly once posed open. Now moving to the horns, I'm sweeping a curved bezier path for each horn with a tapering radius down to a sharp point, then planning gold rings as torus shapes wrapped around points along the horn path.

For the neck, I'm setting up a three-joint bezier sweep with tapered radii and adding a gold collar torus at its base, plus small cheek columns tapering outward from the head.

I'm checking that the neck connects cleanly into the torso's flat cap, then placing flame cards behind the head using spine joint positioning so they peek up around the skull's crown.

Now I'm scattering floating ember sparks around the body at randomized angles and radii, keeping them clear of the arm's reach so they don't clip through limbs, then adding a surface scatter of small studs across the torso skin with a filter to avoid downward-facing normals.

Still writing stud geometry...

I'm defining a lighter basalt color cel for the plates, then planning to scatter similar studs across the arm and leg tubes before positioning the hand geometry as slightly stretched icosahedrons attached to the arm bones.

Now I'm figuring out knuckle spikes on the back of the hand using small hexagonal columns, then placing a gold cuff torus near the wrist by computing the forearm radius at that point, plus a spike detail near the elbow.

Still positioning finger joints...

Confirming the thumb curls inward toward the body while the finger z-range sits forward relative to it, and assigning the digit role with crack paint applied to each finger. Now I'm placing filigree decals on the pauldron surface, positioning them just outside the scaled radius so they sit near the outer edge rather than overlapping it.

Moving on to chest detailing, I'm adding icosahedron shapes scaled flat and wide on each side of the chest to build out pectoral bulk, then planning three rows of small abdominal plates with gaps between them to let the lava glow show through underneath.

Checking part counts stay well under budget, then starting the flame texture SVG shape.

Writing flame layers... Now moving to the tassel texture.

I realize since the card hangs downstream-side up, the tassel appears upside down from that view, so the cap needs to sit at the bottom with strands fanning upward toward the hang point. Writing filigree circle decorations...

Checking the color palette stays under the limit and glancing at the eye glow settings before double-checking part geometry definitions.

Working out the brow extrusion outline, mirroring it correctly across the x-axis for both sides, and setting the extrude thickness and positioning options.

To avoid typecheck issues, I should annotate outline arrays explicitly as OutlinePoint[] rather than relying on inferred number[][] types -- applying the same fix to the loincloth plate outline. Then I'm sanity-checking part counts: roughly 40 lava glow pieces for the columns and about 14 flame cross-cards, keeping triangle counts modest overall.

Now I'm checking the stick/paint/scatter/drape APIs are being used correctly -- colors as Fill, scatter returning Hit arrays, drape building a catmull curve from mirrored points per segment with a lift value. I'm planning the glowRod helper and double-checking the torso surface is built only from the torso sweep part, with back dorsal columns positioned at x=0 near the spine joint to avoid decal collisions, before moving on to the pelvis hip guard details.

Still writing chain and sweep calls...

Still defining frames...
